description: Group sessions share ONE Google Meet event. Today lib/meeting.ts creates one Calendar event per booking (event id derived from the booking id) with the single customer as the only attendee. For GROUP services, Phase 6 requires one shared event per Session: create it once for the first paid attendee, then add each subsequent paid attendee to that SAME event, and give every booking in the session the same meet_link and event_id. Seat counting already happens transactionally in lib/holds.ts and must continue to prevent overselling. This feature covers the first three Phase 6 checklist items: group capacity + one shared event, transactional seat counting (verify/strengthen, do not regress), and adding each paid attendee to the same event and sending them the same link. Depends on FEAT-001 (validation approach). Must land before FEAT-003/FEAT-004 which read the new fields.
steps: Schema: in prisma/schema.prisma add shared-event fields to the Session model so a group's single event is tracked at the session level, not per booking. Add nullable fields: eventId String? @map("event_id"), meetLink String? @map("meet_link"), and a conferenceRequestId or reuse a derived id. Keep per-booking eventId/meetLink on Booking (each attendee still gets the link copied onto their booking for the dashboard and messaging). Follow the existing @map snake_case convention.

Add a hand-written migration prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_group_shared_event/migration.sql that ALTER TABLE "sessions" ADD COLUMN the new columns, mirroring the SQL style in prisma/migrations/20261009000000_google_meet/migration.sql. Use a timestamp later than 20261009000000. Also add an entry consistent with prisma/migrations/migration_lock.toml (do not change the provider).

In lib/meeting.ts, add a session-scoped event id helper (e.g. sessionEventId(sessionId) using the same sha256 hex scheme as calendarEventId but keyed on `session:<id>`). For GROUP services the event id must be derived from the SESSION so all bookings converge on one event; for ONE_TO_ONE keep the existing per-booking calendarEventId behaviour unchanged.

In lib/google.ts, extend GoogleClient to support adding an attendee to an existing event without dropping the others. Add a method such as addAttendee(accessToken, eventId, attendee) or patchEventAttendees that GETs the event, appends the attendee if not already present (dedupe by email), and PATCHes with sendUpdates=all so the new attendee gets the invite while existing attendees are not re-notified unnecessarily. Reuse the existing error classification (classifyCalendarError) and the CalendarEvent shape. Keep insertEvent working for the single-attendee create.

In lib/meeting.ts createMeetingForBooking: branch on service.type. For GROUP: use the session-derived event id; if the session has no eventId yet, insert the event once (summary names the service/group, first paid attendee as attendee) and on success store eventId+meetLink on the SESSION; if the session already has an event, call the new addAttendee path to add THIS booking's customer to the shared event. In both cases copy the session's eventId+meetLink onto the booking and mark it SCHEDULED, then enqueue the confirmation message. Preserve all existing idempotency guarantees (booking already has eventId -> re-enqueue message only; crash-safety via deterministic ids; the updateMany guard that detects a cancelled/refunded booking). Preserve the 60-minute free-Gmail group-call warning that is already logged.

Guard the shared-event create/add against races: two attendees paying at once must not both try to create the event. Use the same approach the codebase already uses (a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the sessions row, or an atomic updateMany with a where-guard on session.eventId null) so exactly one create happens and the rest take the add-attendee path. Mirror the locking style in lib/holds.ts / lib/checkout.ts / lib/payment-webhook.ts.

Verify seat counting still prevents oversell for groups: read lib/holds.ts createHold and confirm activeSeatWhere + the FOR UPDATE on the session row still enforce service.capacity. If the shared-event change introduced any new path that creates bookings or bypasses the capacity check, fix it. Do not weaken the existing 1:1 unique-constraint behaviour.

Update requeuePendingMeetings and reportMeetingFailure in lib/meeting.ts if needed so they remain correct when bookings share an event (e.g. a paid group booking whose session already has an event should get the link via the add-attendee path, not be stuck).

Add/extend tests: create tests/group-meeting.test.ts in the node:test + tsx style (see tests/signature.test.ts). Keep it DB-free by exercising lib/meeting.ts with injected MeetingDeps (the existing overrides parameter) and a fake GoogleClient that records insertEvent vs addAttendee calls. Cover: first group booking inserts exactly one event; a second booking for the same session does NOT insert a second event but adds the attendee; both bookings end up with the same meet_link; a 1:1 booking still uses the per-booking event path. If a test genuinely needs the generated Prisma client or a DB (which is unavailable here), isolate that in a clearly separate test and note it cannot run in this sandbox.

Update doc/06-groups-and-dashboard.md to check off the first three tasks, and update doc/03-google-meet.md's note that 'Phase 6 changes group sessions to one shared event' to reflect that it is now implemented. Add a short 'Phase 6' note to README.md if the Phase list there needs it.
acceptance_criteria: prisma/schema.prisma has session-level shared-event fields and a matching hand-written SQL migration exists under prisma/migrations/ with a timestamp after 20261009000000

For a GROUP service, lib/meeting.ts creates exactly one Calendar event per Session and adds every other paid attendee to that same event; all bookings in the session carry the identical meet_link and event_id
For a ONE_TO_ONE service the existing per-booking event behaviour is unchanged
Concurrent paid attendees for the same group session cannot create two events (serialized via FOR UPDATE / atomic guard following the existing pattern)
Group seat counting still refuses to oversell beyond service.capacity (lib/holds.ts behaviour preserved)
tests/group-meeting.test.ts exists and asserts single-insert + add-attendee + shared link using an injected fake GoogleClient, with no reliance on a live DB
verification: Static validation (no build/test tooling in this sandbox): grep that every new symbol used in lib/meeting.ts (e.g. the add-attendee method, sessionEventId) is actually exported from its module; grep that every Session/Booking field referenced in code (eventId, meetLink) matches prisma/schema.prisma @map names
Confirm the new migration SQL column names exactly match the @map names added to the Session model
Read tests/group-meeting.test.ts and confirm it would fail if the group branch created one event per booking instead of one per session
In a normal environment these would additionally run: `npx prisma generate`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (note in findings that these are CI-only here)
